subject: Capacity safeguard playbook: request for cross-functional alignment
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity safeguard playbook: request for cross-functional alignment

Team —

Quick context: NexaHealth (pilot prospect) just confirmed a pilot start window for mid-Oct and expects bursty inference traffic tied to weekly model retrains. They want a short-term dedicated GPU pool for the pilot plus an exception to our standard autoscale backoff for the first 6 weeks. Procurement also asked for a playbook describing how we will prevent noisy neighbors and ensure SLOs during the pilot.

Asks:
- Can product + infra agree a minimum reserved footprint and guardrails we can commit to in the pilot MOU?
- Ops: what monitoring + rapid-rollback controls do we need in the playbook?
- Sales: I need a concise one-page summary I can share with procurement by EOD Friday (10/1).

Attachments I will paste to the thread: NexaHealth traffic forecast (they sent estimates) and an initial skeleton of a playbook I started.

Important constraints I heard from Nexa: 2x traffic spikes on deploy days, sustained 60% higher qps first 2 weeks. They will not accept >200ms p95 outages.

Thanks — please reply with availability for a 30-minute alignment sync today or tomorrow and any immediate blockers.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity safeguard playbook: request for cross-functional alignment

Vanessa —

Thanks for the heads-up. High level from product: we can offer a temporary dedicated pool with the following initial footprint options: 
- Small: 2x A100 equivalent GPUs (low cost reserve) — supports baseline throughput but fragile on spikes
- Medium: 6x A100 equivalent GPUs — recommended for pilot given retrain spikes
- Large: 12x GPUs — only if procurement will tolerate higher commit costs

Autoscale exception: Product is comfortable supporting a time-limited elevated burst window, but we need Ops/Infra to confirm we can enforce per-tenant QoS (CPU+GPU quotas, KV cache isolation) and an emergency throttling policy.

I'm available at 11:30 PT for a quick sync. I'll bring proposed default commit and rollback thresholds.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Director, Product — Serving
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity safeguard playbook: request for cross-functional alignment

Looping in some operational constraints:
- We can provision a medium pool (6 GPUs) in the us-west region within 48 hours if finance approves a short-term reserve charge.
- To support spikes we will enable prefix caching and increase batch size limits, but that increases tail latency risk unless we lock retrain windows to off-peak hours (we should request this of Nexa).
- Monitoring: we'll include p95/p99 latency dashboards + token-level cost breakdown and an alert that auto-opens a Sev2 if p95 exceeds 200ms for >5 minutes.

Playbook components I suggest:
1) Provisioning checklist (who approves, billing codes)
2) Runbooks for scale-up, emergency throttling, rollback to hosted model variant
3) Communication plan (who notifies customer and CS)
4) Post-pilot debrief and capacity reclamation timeline

I can draft a 1-page playbook summary for procurement if Ben gives any pricing guidance for the 6-GPU medium option.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head, Cloud Ops
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity safeguard playbook: request for cross-functional alignment

Quick technical feasibility and blockers:
- We can enforce a per-tenant GPU quota and soft QoS with our current scheduler. Hard isolation (dedicated hardware) is possible but needs a ticket to infra for allocation lead time.
- KV cache isolation: straightforward if we create tenant-scoped caches; will add an incremental 8–12% memory usage per node.
- Autoscale exception: we can accept a 6-week elevated burst window but require a rollback hook that flips traffic to a hosted, lower-throughput model variant (automated) if errors spike or if p95 breaches threshold for >10 minutes.

Action items for me:
- Create a reserved_pool_matrix.csv that maps footprint -> estimated sustained throughput -> estimated cost delta. (Attached)
- Put together a short runbook for the rollback hook and automated throttling (will link INF-9342).

Attachments referenced: reserved_pool_matrix.csv (csv, 14KB)

— Dev
Dev Patel | Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime

Subject: Fwd: NexaHealth pilot details + traffic forecast (for playbook)

Forwarding the note I got this morning from Natalie at Nexa with the forecast and procurement expectations. This is what procurement will use to judge our proposal. Please pull the numbers you used into the one-pager.

----- Forwarded message -----
From: Natalie Brown <natalie.b@nexahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 07:49:00 -0700
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Subject: NexaHealth pilot details + traffic forecast

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again — attached is the week-by-week forecast for the pilot and our procurement questions:
- Can Redwood commit to no more than 200ms p95 on production calls during the pilot?
- What isolation guarantees can you make if we run retrains every Tuesday at 03:00 PT?
- What happens if sustained traffic exceeds the forecast by 50%?

A few clarifying notes: initial traffic is modest; spikes occur on model deploy day and on EHR ingestion batch days. We are open to a short-term reserved capacity fee for guaranteed isolation.

Best,
Natalie Brown
Head of ML Platform | NexaHealth
natalie.b@nexahealth.com
